The input checks, starting every team at 0 so zero-desk teams appear in order, and using Fraction for exact comparisons are all good changes. But the diff reverses the tie-break: the sort key now uses `-headcounts[team]`, so ties go to the SMALLER team. The docstring, which the teammate named as the source of truth, says ties go to the team with the larger headcount.

The reversal appears to be there only to make test_quarterly_floor_plan pass. Worked by hand (60/30/16, 6 desks): at desk 2, platform (60) and design (30) tie at 30, and at desk 6 they tie again at 15. Under the documented rule platform wins both, giving platform 4, design 1, support 1. The test expects 3/2/1, which only happens if the smaller team wins ties. So that test contradicts the docstring. The rest of the suite doesn't depend on the tie-break, and the equal-headcount case falls back to list order either way.

Please keep the tie-break as documented, `(Fraction(...), headcounts[team])`, and flag the conflicting test to the teammate rather than quietly changing behavior to match it. There's also no PR description, so the change isn't explained anywhere.
